The Laravel Boost guidelines are specifically curated by Laravel maintainers for this application. These guidelines should be followed closely to enhance the user's satisfaction building Laravel applications.

Packages: laravel/framework v12, laravel/prompts v0, laravel/mcp v0, laravel/pint v1, laravel/sail v1, phpunit/phpunit v11.

You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application. When creating or editing a file, check sibling files for the correct structure, approach, naming. Use descriptive names for variables and methods. Check for existing components to reuse before writing a new one. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works. Stick to existing directory structure - don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.

Use Laravel Boost MCP tools. Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command. Use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs. Use `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; use `database-query` for read-only database access; use `browser-logs` for recent browser logs. You must use `search-docs` to search Laravel-ecosystem documentation before other approaches and before code changes. Do not add package names to queries.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even if it has one line. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations and appropriate PHP parameter type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless there is something _very complex going on.

Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files. If you're creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:class`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and pass correct `--options`. Prefer Eloquent relationships and `Model::query()` over raw queries, `DB::`, or manual joins; prevent N+1 with eager loading. Always create Form Request classes for validation. Use queued jobs with `ShouldQueue` for time-consuming operations. Use named routes and `route()`. Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. When creating tests, use `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; use `--unit` for unit tests. Use `php artisan make:test --phpunit {name}`. No middleware files in `app/Http/Middleware/`. `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware, exceptions, and routing. `bootstrap/providers.php` contains application providers. **No app\Console\Kernel.php**. **Commands auto-register**. When modifying a column, the migration must include all previously defined attributes.
